claims.statement: Indian Gross Domestic Health Insurance premium expected to grow at 22.48% CAGR during FY22-FY28E
Total premiums under management reached Rs. 19,050 crores as of March 31, 2024, up 30.7% YoY.
Group premiums grew 30.4% YoY to Rs. 16,709 crores; retail premiums grew 33.2% YoY to Rs. 2,341 crores.
FY24 operating EBITDA margin was 21% vs 23-24% historically; Q4 FY24 margin improved to 22.2% as acquisition synergies kick in.
Management expects margins to return to 23-24% range as integrations of Mayfair, Medvantage, Raksha complete over next 2-3 quarters.
Tech spend ~3-4% of revenue annually; platform investment Rs. 10 crores capitalized as of Mar'23, ~Rs. 8-9 crores for UK platform in FY24.
Depreciation & amortization up Rs. 18 crores from acquisitions (Rs. 10 crores customer relationships, Rs. 8 crores assets); March quarter run-rate is new base.
Staff cost stable at 40-41% of revenue despite volume doubling; technology automation drives productivity.
Effective tax rate ~16% in FY24 due to one-time benefits; normalized ETR 21-22% for forecasting.
Health Insurance premium expected to grow ~23% CAGR FY22-FY28E

Annual technology spend 5%-7% of Revenue

Total premium under management reached Rs 7,076 crores as of June 30, 2025, up 18.5% YoY.
Group premium grew 20.4% YoY; retail premium grew 0.2% YoY.
Group retention at 93.4% including quality-of-revenue calls; over 10,000 corporate accounts managed.
Added over Rs 1,000 crores of new corporate premiums in Q1, one of the largest quarters for new wins.
Private and SAHI retail premiums grew nearly 89% YoY; now constitute 42% of retail premiums.
International business (Mayfair) revenue grew 35.6% YoY.
Government segment saw healthy growth with renewed emphasis on administrator choice in schemes.
Processed over 22 lakh claims in group and retail business in Q1.
Quarterly technology spend is 5-7% of revenue as the company doubles down on investments.
Fraud, waste, and abuse savings reached Rs 160 crores in Q1, up from Rs 50 crores a year ago (3x improvement); AI-led detection now 80% of all frauds detected.
Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 22% in Q1 FY26 from a low of 20.7% in H1 FY24; PAT margin at 11.4%.
Steady-state TPA EBITDA margin target remains 23-24%; Paramount consolidation to impact consolidated margins by 200-250 bps for 5-6 quarters.
Technology services gross margins expected to be better than core TPA margins due to reuse of engineering/infrastructure and no people pass-through costs.
No forward guidance given; company aims to grow at industry rate or faster; consolidated financials with Paramount from Q2.

Average claim size growth at 4.4% vs industry medical inflation of 10-12%.

Management targets return to 22-23% EBITDA margin in core business over 4-5 quarters as Paramount integration completes.
Paramount customer relationship amortization ~Rs. 3.5 Cr per quarter; total intangible assets from acquisition ~Rs. 120 Cr amortized over longer term.
Depreciation and amortization spike due to Paramount PPA intangible creation; run rate expected to continue for few years.
Technology fraud, waste and abuse prevention delivered Rs. 230 Cr savings in H1 FY26, up 50% YoY.
SaaS business at higher gross margin than TPA; expected to be margin-accretive at steady state in 4-5 quarters (2 quarters in).
Service charges always on net premium (excluding GST); GST rate changes do not affect revenue base.
Management expects majority of structural integration of Paramount to be complete, with disciplined execution over next 2-3 quarters to return to core EBITDA margins
